headline: Avoiding Common Mistakes in Your Luxury Condo Sale Closing in Broward County

publisher.name: Kelby Contreras - Realty ONE Group Evolution

articleBody:
Selling a luxury condo in Broward County can be exciting, but the closing process has unique complexities, especially when dealing with condominium associations. It's easy to overlook crucial details that can lead to delays or even jeopardize your sale. From association documents to specific move-out procedures, navigating these waters smoothly is all about preparation and attention to detail. Getting it wrong can mean headaches, lost time, and even financial penalties.

Here are some common mistakes and how to avoid them:

- **Ordering Association Documents Too Late:** Many buyers have a limited review period for condominium documents. Ordering the resale package or estoppel statement at the last minute can cause significant delays and may even give the buyer a reason to back out. _How to avoid it: Order these documents as soon as your property goes under contract, or even proactively before listing if allowed by your association._
- **Relying on Outdated Information:** Association fees, rules, or even litigation can change. Using an old resale package or assuming information is current can lead to surprises. _How to avoid it: Always ensure you have the most recent documents directly from the association management or its authorized portal._
- **Overlooking Special Assessments or Violations:** Failing to disclose or verify pending special assessments, violations, or planned capital projects can be a big problem. Buyers and lenders need to know about these. _How to avoid it: Thoroughly review all association documents and disclose any known issues to your agent and buyer upfront._
- **Ignoring Transfer and Move-in Requirements:** Many luxury condo buildings have strict rules for moving out, including elevator reservations, transfer fees, and even buyer approval processes. _How to avoid it: Get a clear understanding of all move-out and transfer requirements from your association well in advance of closing._
- **Miscalculating Dues and Assessment Prorations:** Incorrectly prorating association dues, special assessments, or other shared costs can lead to disputes at closing. _How to avoid it: Work with your agent and title company to ensure all prorations are accurately calculated based on the closing date._
- **Assuming Lender Acceptance of Documents:** A buyer’s mortgage lender may have specific requirements for condominium project review, and not all association documents will satisfy them without further clarification. _How to avoid it: Encourage your buyer to have their lender review association documents early in the process and address any questions promptly._

What to Do Next
